What Okyo collects, where it goes, and how to delete it

## The short version

Okyo can offer optional sign-in with Apple or Google through Clerk. Your recipes, grocery lists, cooking progress, and dietary settings are stored on this device, not in an Okyo recipe database. A sign-in provider keeps the account information needed to let you sign in, and RevenueCat receives an account identifier to manage subscription access. Two other things leave the device: the food photo or dish description you send for analysis, and the preferences needed to shape the recipe. Those are processed and returned; Okyo does not build a server-side recipe profile from them.

## Your profile and onboarding answers

During onboarding Okyo asks for a first name, a name for your fox companion, a main goal, and — depending on that goal — answers about eating habits, weekly spending, or protein and calorie targets. These are saved on this device. They are used to personalize screens and to shape the recipes Okyo generates. They are not sold, and they are not sent anywhere except as described under “What is sent for analysis”.

## Food preferences, allergies and dietary restrictions

If you record allergies, restrictions, foods you avoid, or dislikes, they are stored on this device and included with a recipe request so the recipe can be adapted around them. Treat these as health-related information about you and share only what you want used.

Okyo cannot guarantee that a generated recipe is free of an allergen. Always check ingredient labels yourself.

## Nutrition targets and progress

Calorie and macronutrient targets you set, the meals you mark completed, and the savings and macro totals Okyo shows you are calculated and stored on this device. They are estimates from recipe data, not a medical or dietetic record.

## What is sent for analysis

When you scan a dish, the photo you took or chose is sent to the Okyo service. The Okyo service passes it to an AI provider (OpenRouter, which routes the request to the model vendor Okyo has configured) so the dish can be identified and a recipe written. If you describe a dish in words instead, the text is sent the same way and no photo is involved.

Relevant recipe context travels with the request: the cooking mode, servings, your dietary preferences and any nutrition targets, and — when you correct a result or ask a question — the text you typed and the recipe being corrected.

## How long the photo is kept

On this device: the photo is copied into Okyo’s own app storage so a saved recipe keeps its picture. It stays there until you delete the recipe or use “Delete my data”.

On the Okyo service: the photo is held in memory only for as long as the request takes. Okyo does not write it to a database or a log file. Okyo does keep a short-lived result cache keyed by a one-way fingerprint of the image, so scanning the same photo twice within a day reuses the earlier answer; the cache holds the recipe, not the picture.

At the AI provider: retention is set by that provider, not by Okyo. Okyo will not claim a provider deletes your image immediately, because Okyo cannot verify that from its own code.

## Recipes, groceries and cooking progress

Generated recipes, edits and corrections, the recipes you like, grocery selections and checked-off items, Cook Mode progress, completed meals, and the feedback you leave are all stored on this device so the app can restore them. They are not uploaded to an Okyo recipe profile database.

## Analytics

When enabled for a build, PostHog receives explicit app and screen activity, coarse onboarding and sign-in progress, scan outcomes, recipe actions, tour progress, settings, account-deletion outcomes, and coarse error/performance events. Properties are restricted to app version, platform, build environment, broad screen/flow categories, approved action/outcome values, and bounded durations. Okyo does not send answers, names, email addresses, account/provider IDs, session IDs, photos, recipes, allergy or health answers, signatures, typed text, IP address properties, or raw API responses. Events use a random app-generated analytics ID, not an account or app session ID; profile processing is disabled, and the ID is rotated after account deletion. The API has a separate optional PostHog integration for coarse AI-operation metrics. The app sends no automatic text capture, screenshots, or screen recordings. Sentry is separately configured for filtered crash diagnostics. PostHog project settings must disable IP capture.

## Diagnostics and logs

The Okyo service records operational entries such as whether a request contained an image, its size, which model answered, and whether the result was rejected. Image contents, meal descriptions and correction text are stripped before anything is written. Development builds additionally print debugging detail to the developer’s own machine; release builds do not.

## Notifications

Notifications are optional and off unless you turn them on. Cooking timers and reminders are scheduled by this device. No notification content is sent to a server, and Okyo does not use a push service.

## Purchases

Subscriptions are sold and processed by the App Store, not by Okyo. Okyo uses RevenueCat to ask whether your subscription is currently active. Okyo never sees or handles your card details. Purchase identifiers and receipts are not placed into analytics or product logs.

## Who else receives data

Only the parties needed to run the features you use: the Okyo service, PostHog when analytics is enabled, the AI provider that identifies dishes and writes recipes, and Apple plus RevenueCat for subscriptions. Okyo does not sell personal information and does not share it for targeted advertising.

## International processing

The AI provider and the subscription services operate internationally, so a request may be processed outside your country. The exact regions Okyo’s own service runs in are not yet fixed and will be stated here before launch.

## Children

Okyo is a general-audience cooking app and is not directed at children. A minimum age has not yet been set; it will be stated here and enforced in the store listing before launch.

## Your choices

You can edit or clear your dietary preferences and nutrition targets at any time, turn notifications on or off, delete every piece of Okyo data on this device from Settings › Privacy & data › Delete all my data, and delete a signed-in account from the same screen. Deleting data or an account does not cancel a subscription — only the App Store can do that.

## Regional rights

Depending on where you live you may have rights to access, correct, delete or port your information, or to object to certain processing. Most Okyo content is exercised directly on the device: it is in the app, and deletion is available from Settings. A signed-in user can also delete the account record through Settings. See “Regional privacy rights” for the detail, and “Privacy requests and deletion” for how to reach a human.

## Contact

For privacy questions, email Okyo at support.okyo@gmail.com.

Extra rights that may apply where you live

### Read this alongside the Privacy Policy

These notes add region-specific detail. They do not all apply to everyone — each section says who it is for. The countries Okyo will actually be offered in have not been finalized, so this section will be narrowed to those markets before launch.

### A note that changes everything below

Okyo has no accounts and stores your information on your own device. Okyo cannot look you up, cannot connect a request to a person, and holds no server-side copy to hand over. That means most access, correction and portability requests are answered by the app itself: what Okyo holds about you is what is on your screen, and deletion is one tap in Settings.

### Europe and the United Kingdom (GDPR / UK GDPR)

If you are in the EEA, Switzerland or the UK you have rights to access, rectify, erase, restrict and port your personal data, to object to processing, and to complain to your data protection authority. The lawful bases Okyo relies on, and whether Okyo needs a representative in the EU or UK, are being assessed with counsel and will be stated here before Okyo is offered in those markets. Okyo does not use your data for automated decisions with legal effects.

### California and other US states

If you are a resident of California, Colorado, Connecticut, Virginia or another US state with a consumer privacy law, you may have rights to know, delete, correct and port your personal information, and to opt out of sale, sharing for cross-context behavioural advertising, and profiling. Okyo does not sell personal information, does not share it for targeted advertising, and does not profile you for those purposes, so there is no opt-out to offer — if that ever changes, an opt-out will be added before it does. Okyo will not discriminate against you for exercising a right.

### Washington State (My Health My Data)

Dietary restrictions, allergies and nutrition targets can count as consumer health data under Washington law. Okyo keeps that information on your device, does not sell it, and does not use it for advertising. Whether Okyo is a regulated entity under that law, and what a separate consumer-health-data notice must say, is being assessed with counsel.

### Canada, including Quebec

If you are in Canada you may have rights of access and correction under PIPEDA, and Quebec’s Law 25 adds further rights including portability. Okyo’s Canadian obligations are being confirmed with counsel.

### Australia

If you are in Australia, the Australian Privacy Principles may give you rights of access and correction, and the Australian Consumer Law gives you consumer guarantees that cannot be excluded. Whether Okyo is an APP entity depends on business facts not yet settled.

### How to raise a request

See “Privacy requests and deletion”. Because Okyo cannot identify you, a request that would require Okyo to find “your” data on a server cannot be fulfilled — there is no such data — and Okyo will tell you that plainly rather than pretending to search.

How to see, correct, export or delete your data

### Access — you already have it

Everything Okyo holds about you is in this app, on this device. Your profile and goal are in Settings, your preferences in Dietary preferences and Nutrition targets, your recipes in Liked, your lists in Grocery, and your totals in Stats & progress. There is no hidden server-side profile to request.

### Correction

Edit anything directly: your name and fox name, your goal, your dietary preferences and nutrition targets, and any generated recipe. A wrong dish result can be corrected in place without rescanning.

### Deletion

Settings › Privacy & data › Delete all my data removes every Okyo record on this device: profile and fox name, goal and onboarding answers, dietary preferences and nutrition targets, saved and generated recipes, grocery lists and checked items, Cook Mode progress, completed meals, savings and macro totals, notification preferences, your recorded permission choices, and the stored scan images. A signed-in user can also choose Delete account from that screen to remove the Clerk account record and request deletion of the associated RevenueCat customer record. It can be run as many times as you like.

It does not cancel your subscription, and it cannot remove records Apple or RevenueCat keep about a purchase — those are their records, under their retention rules. Uninstalling Okyo also removes the app’s stored data.

### Export

A data export file is not built yet, and Okyo will not pretend otherwise. Because the data is all on this device and visible in the app, there is nothing Okyo is holding back from you.

### Objection and consent withdrawal

Every optional processing in Okyo is something you switch on: notifications, camera access and photo access. Turn any of them off in your device Settings, or turn notification categories off inside Okyo, and the corresponding processing stops. Okyo runs no analytics, advertising or tracking to object to.

### Opting out of sale or targeted advertising

There is nothing to opt out of. Okyo does not sell personal information and does not share it for targeted advertising.

### If you would rather talk to a person

For privacy questions, email Okyo at support.okyo@gmail.com. Signed-in accounts can be deleted in the app. A person requesting help with a third-party record, such as an Apple purchase, may need to contact that provider directly.

## How long Okyo keeps things

Retention for each kind of data

### On this device

Your profile, preferences, nutrition targets, recipes, grocery lists, cooking progress, completed meals and totals stay on this device until you delete them or remove the app. Okyo does not expire them on a timer.

### Scan photos on this device

A photo you scan is copied into Okyo’s app storage. A photo not attached to any saved recipe is cleaned up when its scan session ends. “Delete my data” removes the whole folder.

### On the Okyo service

The Okyo service holds no long-term store of your data. During and shortly after a scan it keeps short-lived working state in memory only: analysis context for 15 minutes, a generated recipe for 24 hours so it can be enriched or corrected, a result cache for 24 hours, and a rejected-image result for 1 hour. All of it is lost when the service restarts. Image bytes are never written to disk.

### Logs

Operational log entries record what happened — sizes, models, outcomes — with image data, meal descriptions and correction text stripped out. A production log retention period has not yet been fixed and will be stated here before launch.

### At the AI provider

Okyo cannot state the AI provider’s retention period from its own code and will not guess. This will be filled in from the provider’s contract terms before launch.

### Purchases

Apple and RevenueCat keep subscription records under their own retention rules. Okyo does not control them, and cannot delete them on your behalf.

## Service providers

Who else touches your data, and why

### AI provider — OpenRouter

Receives the food photo or dish description, plus recipe context such as servings, cooking mode and your dietary preferences, and routes it to the model Okyo has configured so a dish can be identified and a recipe written. This is a service provider acting on Okyo’s instructions for that purpose. The model vendor behind the routing is a further processor in the same chain.

### Subscriptions — Apple

Sells the subscription, takes payment, and issues refunds. Apple is an independent party with its own privacy policy, not a service provider acting for Okyo. Okyo never sees your payment details.

### Entitlement checks — RevenueCat

Tells Okyo whether the subscription attached to your Apple ID is currently active, so the app can unlock paid features and restore a purchase. It receives purchase and device identifiers from the store, not your recipes, photos or dietary information.

### What is not here

No advertising network, crash-reporting service, marketing or email platform, or data broker is integrated. Analytics transmission is disabled unless the publisher deliberately configures it; if enabled, its provider will be listed here and disclosed before release.

### Hosting

Where Okyo’s own service will be hosted has not been finalized. The provider and region will be listed here before launch.
